Abstract:Training-free activation guardrails such as kNNGuard score prompts by comparing last-token LLM hidden states (the Layer Ensemble branch, kNNGuard LE) and sentence embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, Embedding-kNN) against a small reference bank (50 examples per class), combining the two branches into a Fused Ensemble (kNNGuard FE). While effective on short inputs (up to 256 tokens), standard kNNGuard degrades substantially on long inputs (over 1000 tokens): averaged across Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma-4-E4B-it, kNNGuard LE AUROC drops from 0.742 (0.777 and 0.706) to 0.554 (0.587 and 0.521) on Content Harm Moderation (Aegis-2.0), and from 0.994 (0.995 and 0.992) to 0.556 (0.598 and 0.513) on RAG Hallucination Detection (HaluBench). We trace this degradation to three causes: (1) hidden-state drift as sequence length increases, (2) hard 256-token truncation in MiniLM, and (3) signal dilution when a long document is compressed into a single final-token vector. We then evaluate three training-free adaptations: a Length-Routed Dual Bank, a long-context embedding model (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B), and Strided Window Pooling across intermediate token positions. On Content Harm Moderation, dual-bank routing and strided window pooling raise long-context kNNGuard LE AUROC from 0.554 to 0.828 (+0.274 AUROC) and fused kNNGuard FE AUROC from 0.721 to 0.886 (+0.164 AUROC) with no latency overhead from bank routing. On RAG Hallucination Detection, where the guardrail must verify logical consistency between a generated answer and a retrieved passage, sentence-embedding kNN remains near random chance across all lengths, while length-matched LLM hidden states (kNNGuard LE) recover medium-length detection (AUROC = 0.853) but remain limited on over-1000-token passages (AUROC = 0.607) due to final-token dilution over long contexts.

Abstract:Muon constructs matrix updates by applying a matrix-sign transformation to momentum. A common route to accelerating Muon is to modify the gradient or momentum before this transformation. We explore a complementary direction: refining the parameter step while retaining Muon’s momentum recursion. Derived from the parameter subproblem of the ADMM-Inspired Momentum framework, AIMuon uses the gradient–momentum residual to correct the tentative spectral step. The residual undergoes a separate matrix-sign transformation, while spectral–nuclear duality determines the relative weighting of the momentum and residual directions. In practice, both directions are approximated with Newton–Schulz iterations and their combination is rescaled to match Muon’s update magnitude. We establish a stochastic stationarity bound for the corresponding exact iteration. On GPT-2-small, GPT-2-medium, and Qwen3-0.6B, AIMuon reaches Muon’s final validation loss with 8.98%, 10.05%, and 6.49% fewer optimization steps, respectively, while achieving lower final validation loss than Muon, Muon-Nesterov, and MONA.

作者: Yiyang Chen,Kohei Hatano,Eiji Takimoto

Abstract:We study online learning for minimizing maximum tardiness (\OMMT) in single-machine scheduling. In each round, the learner selects a permutation of (n) fixed jobs, representing a schedule. The environment then reveals a processing time and a due date for each job, and the learner incurs a vector-valued loss whose components correspond to the tardiness of the individual jobs. The goal of the learner is to minimize (\alpha)-regret, the difference between the learner’s maximum cumulative tardiness and (\alpha) times that of the best fixed permutation in hindsight, for as small (\alpha) as possible. We investigate OMMT under both stochastic and adversarial environments. In the stochastic setting, we prove that the expected (1)-regret of the Follow-the-Leader (FTL) algorithm is ( O!\left(\fracn\log n\Delta^2\right) ), together with a corresponding high-probability bound, where (\Delta) is a distribution-dependent gap parameter. At round (t \in \1,\dots,T\), FTL runs in (O(tn^2)) time and (O(tn)) space. In the adversarial setting, we prove that, for any (0c\log_2 n/16), the (\alpha)-regret is (\Omega(T)) whenever (\alpha\log_2 n/16-c). We then reduce OMMT to a surrogate online learning problem and apply Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader (FTPL), obtaining an expected (\alpha)-regret bound of (O(n^2\sqrtT)) for (\alpha=O(\log n)). Thus, the logarithmic dependence of (\alpha) on (n) is tight up to constant factors. Each FTPL update admits a mixed-integer programming formulation whose size is polynomial in (n) and (t). Abstract:Early time-series classification (ETSC) balances predictive performance against the amount of observed data. In multimodal settings, modality-associated and fused branches may differ in predictive ability at the same observed prefix, motivating joint decisions about when to stop and which branch should provide the final prediction. We propose COMPASS, a two-stage framework that preserves two modality-associated temporal branches and one fusion branch. The first stage combines cross-modal feature exchange and gated fusion with branch-wise supervision at every prefix. The second stage optimizes a shared four-action controller to continue observation or terminate through one of the frozen branches. Experiments on six physiological and wearable datasets compare COMPASS with multimodal adaptations of five ETSC baselines. COMPASS achieves the best average ranks in accuracy-earliness harmonic mean, AUROC, and earliness within this comparison set. At identical learned stopping times, branch selection improves mean accuracy over fusion readout on five of the six datasets, with gains of 2.35 and 2.16 percentage points on ISRUC-Sleep and UCDDB, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work on joint stopping and branch selection for multimodal early time series classification.

Abstract:Co-folding models predict the structures of proteins and their bound ligands, but their accuracy varies across targets. Their usefulness therefore depends on knowing which predictions a user can trust. Confidence scores are intended to guide that choice. However, across seven co-folding models, we show that confidence-based selection offers little improvement over choosing a prediction at random. For approximately three-quarters of structures, predictions are either exclusively correct or incorrect, leaving no opportunity for ranking to change the outcome. Moreover, high confidence does not reliably discriminate correct top-ranked predictions from incorrect ones. We find that structural agreement among predictions is a more accurate measure of likely success than current confidence scores. We capture this with the Concentration of Repeated Ensembles (CORE) Score, which combines cluster tightness with ensemble support. CORE Score discriminates top-1 success and oracle success, achieving mean ROC AUCs of 0.866 and 0.838, compared to 0.757 and 0.759 for ipTM. CORE Score also outperforms training set similarity measures, including ligand Tanimoto, protein sequence, and Runs N’ Poses similarity, despite requiring no experimental ligand pose. Structural agreement is therefore a practical indicator of reliability and a baseline for evaluating future confidence estimators, without requiring an additional trained uncertainty estimator.

Abstract:We study spatio-temporal forecasting in networked systems under specified actions. The challenge is to capture the action’s effects without predicting spurious changes in unaffected regions. However, direct supervision and evaluation of these effects require paired futures with and without the action, whereas observational trajectories reveal only the realized future. We introduce PairST, a benchmark comprising six datasets across traffic, power transmission and water distribution, with paired reference and intervened futures simulated from the same system state. These pairs enable separate evaluation of affected-region forecast accuracy and quiet-region response error. We further propose ActionST, which forecasts the intervened future by writing an explicit response onto an intervention-independent reference forecast. Specifically, node-time addressing constructs a query for each response position, a state-conditioned response writer computes candidate responses, and a graph-aware locality gate controls their strength. Experiments on six datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of ActionST at new action targets, with the lowest mean absolute error on five datasets and the best average rank. Our source code and the PairST benchmark are available at this https URL.

Abstract:Motor decoding from electroencephalography (EEG) supports non-invasive brain-computer interfaces, yet existing methods either rely on costly cue-based trials and coarse categorical labels or use pretraining objectives that do not directly capture how movement unfolds, limiting their ability to learn transferable motor representations. To this end, we propose the Mind World Model (MWM), a framework that learns motor EEG representations from scalable naturalistic EEG and egocentric video without action annotations. MWM treats EEG observed up to the current frame as the latent action of a world model: a mind model encodes the EEG, and a world model uses it to predict the representation of a future frame, yielding a movement-grounded pretraining objective. We further introduce the Lateralization-Aware Transformer (LAT), which uses frame averaging to separate shared bilateral from side-specific lateral features, encoding hemispheric correspondence to reduce the burden of learning left-right relationships from data. MWM pretraining produces two models: a mind model for downstream motor decoding and a world model that can be adapted to prediction conditioned on real actions, opening a scalable and flexible path to collect egocentric data for embodied AI. Across 9 classification and 7 regression tasks, the mind model improves task-averaged balanced accuracy by 5.9% and Pearson correlation by 16.2% relative to the strongest baseline in each task family. Compared with an inverse-dynamics latent-action baseline, the world model achieves lower prediction error and benefits 3.3 times more from matched real actions within recordings and 4.7 times more on held-out subjects.

Abstract:A digital twin of a patient in intensive care would forecast the patient’s course and what a treatment would change. Generative event models, trained to continue a patient’s electronic health record (EHR), have been proposed as a path toward such twins. We trained TWICE, a 79M-parameter decoder-only transformer, on the ICU records of one academic health system (127,332 training patients and 1.57 billion tokens). We evaluated it on clinical prediction tasks, generation fidelity, individual trajectories and counterfactual validation. Reading 19 clinical outcomes off 50 simulated futures, with no task-specific training, TWICE matched the best of 144 supervised configurations on held-out patients (mean AUROC 0.836 vs. 0.834). It led on events that change care within a day and trailed on death. With the training data fixed, more and longer simulated futures were worth more than a 6.8-fold larger model. Its generated records matched real ones closely and were as specific to each patient as its own variability allowed. Its predicted risk rose as events approached. Abstract:Learning for optimal power flow (OPF) has recently been advocated to accelerate OPF solutions by using a pre-trained neural network (NN) to predict directly from given inputs such as the load demand. Abstract:Advanced machine-learning models are increasingly used for property valuation in tax assessment. Abstract:A circle and a quartic superellipse have the same homology, but their defining equations have degrees two and four, respectively. We study this algebraic distinction for point-cloud distributions. For a probability measure \mu on \Omega=[-1,1]^d and an orthonormal polynomial feature map \phi_m of degree m , the moment matrix G_m(\mu)=\mathbbE_X\sim\mu[\phi_m(X)\phi_m(X)^\top] satisfies c^\top G_m(\mu)c=\mathbbE_\mu[f_c(X)^2] , so coefficient directions associated with its small eigenvalues represent low-degree polynomials that nearly vanish on \mu . Counting these near-relation directions across degree m and the tolerance \varepsilon gives a two-parameter integer signature. We call this representation distributional algebro-geometric persistence (dAGP), the population counterpart of the point-cloud algebro-geometric persistence (AGP) construction. For empirical measures, dAGP is the sample-normalised counterpart of point-cloud AGP. We also show that \mu\mapsto G_m(\mu) is Lipschitz in the 1 -Wasserstein distance, so its ordered eigenvalues vary Lipschitz-continuously under transport of mass, while its threshold counts remain unchanged under perturbations satisfying a spectral-margin condition. We give an explicit support-localised Lipschitz constant and identify the regime in which the resulting guarantee is informative. Experimentally, the population noise-floor prediction agrees with the finite-sample mean to 0.1% , within sampling error. At a selected tolerance, relation onset orders the conic, quartic, and non-algebraic closed curves, while their count profiles distinguish them from the two-dimensional control. Calibration identifies an empirical tolerance range. A 100 -repetition sensitivity study quantifies onset recovery and shows that the count grid and two continuous spectral baselines nearly saturate the four-family discrimination task.

Abstract:Several methods in statistics and machine learning represent a predictive distribution as an equally weighted mixture of models, or particles, trained via the mixture predictive likelihood. However, we prove that the mixture predictive likelihood is poorly suited to gradient-based optimisation, because it does not identify how the mixture is decomposed across particles, so that a poorly matched particle can be starved of training signal. As a remedy, we study a convex combination between the individual risk, i.e. the average log loss of the individual particles, and the mixture risk. At the particle level, this regularised risk imposes a reverse-KL barrier on the responsibilities of the particles, so that no particle can be starved of training signal. These phenomena are illustrated in two case studies: In the first, a predictively-oriented posterior is computed using mean-field Langevin dynamics, and the numerics are well-behaved only when our regularisation is employed. In the second, ensembles of low-rank adapters are jointly fine-tuned on large language models, across four backbones and eight multiple-choice reasoning benchmarks; direct minimisation of the mixture risk leads to responsibility starvation, whose severity decreases as the competence of the backbone increases, whereas our regularised estimator attains a lower held-out mixture risk on every backbone considered.

Abstract:We develop self-supervised methods for training Recursive Quadrature Filter (RQF) encoders on unlabeled time series. Abstract:Traffic forecasting models are typically evaluated under ideal conditions with complete data. Abstract:World models based on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) learn from pixels to predict the outcome of actions in a latent space. Abstract:Federated fine-tuning of foundation models with low-rank adapters (LoRA) is typically reconciled by averaging locally trained adapters. In cross-device settings, where participants hold heterogeneous data and join or leave asynchronously, averaging is poorly suited: locally trained adapters are not identifiable up to permutation, and averages of adapters trained on dissimilar data can be uninformative or unstable. We propose a simple idea called federated library-based adaptation (LEAN), which replaces averaging altogether. We prove that, in a synchronous setting, LEAN converges to a neighborhood of a stationary point, with the shuffle canceling data heterogeneity at first order. Across image and text fine-tuning benchmarks, LEAN outperforms averaging-based baselines in most settings with substantially less communication, and remains effective under heavy data heterogeneity, where averaging-based methods fail to reach nontrivial accuracy, and under heavy asynchrony, where they degrade substantially.

Abstract:Causal Abstraction defines a notion of \emphequivalence between a neural network and an algorithm, thus serving as a powerful framework for mechanistic interpretability. Abstract:Electronic health records (EHRs) contain rich health information for uncovering latent patient representations and clinically meaningful subgroups. 点击查看摘要

Abstract:We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.

[LG-78] Autonomous quantum machine learning via Riemannian gradient-based optimization

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27815
作者: Kasidit Srimahajariyapong,Thiparat Chotibut,Suwannachad Suwannajitt,Tithivich Paka,Ricard Puig,Yudai Suzuki,Marek Gluza,Zoë Holmes,Supanut Thanasilp
类目: Quantum Physics (quant-ph); Statistical Mechanics (cond-mat.stat-mech); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Machine Learning (stat.ML)
*备注: 18+27 pages, 3+3 figures

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Quantum machine learning models typically rely on repeated quantum measurements and classical optimization during training, making the quantum-to-classical information-extraction process a fundamental bottleneck for scalability. We propose a framework for autonomous self-training quantum machine learning, based on Riemannian gradient optimization, in which the optimization proceeds entirely within the quantum domain without requiring quantum measurements or classical feedback. We derive the Riemannian gradient update rules for a broad class of learning tasks and identify sufficient conditions under which the resulting training dynamics can be realized fully autonomously. Within this regime, we establish an exponential convergence guarantee, in the training iterations, for sufficiently small step sizes, and further analyze the training cost in terms of the growth of the circuit depth. Importantly, we further show that the trained model can automatically discover symmetries hidden in the training data without \textita priori specification. For the canonical examples of quantum phase classification and unitary learning with a hidden symmetry, our numerical study indicates that learning can be achieved at low circuit depths with only a few distinct training examples. Our results thus establish autonomous quantum machine learning as a promising paradigm that removes the classical optimization loop while retaining strong theoretical guarantees and practical performances.

[LG-79] Budgeted Subset Selection with a Transferable Learned Value Model

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27751
作者: Jade Lejeune Herman,Johan A.K. Suykens,Peter Goos
类目: Machine Learning (stat.ML); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
*备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Subset selection is a fundamental task in machine learning, statistics and combinatorial optimisation, with applications in active learning, band selection, input selection and experimental design. The utility of a subset depends on information revealed only after the selection, such as labels or responses, and on interactions among selected candidates. Existing approaches combine value estimation and redundancy control in application-specific ways, which limits their use in other domains. This paper introduces Subset Acquisition with Learned Value Estimates and Search (SALVES), a framework that decomposes subset selection into two components. First, a value model is trained by supervised learning on tasks where the hidden information is known. On a new task, it predicts the utility each candidate would add to the current selection. Second, a selection step chooses the subset from these predictions, typically by simulated annealing with a diversity term penalising redundancy. The value model transfers to new classes, pretrained networks, datasets and sensors, and from synthetic to real data. On the four applications, SALVES matches or outperforms application-specific baselines on average. It requires substantially fewer bands for equal accuracy and remains reliable in input selection where individual baselines fail.

[LG-80] Can pretrained Transformers deliver semiparametrically efficient inference?

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27666
作者: Han Yan,Jin Zhu,Chengchun Shi,Tengyao Wang
类目: Machine Learning (stat.ML); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Statistics Theory (math.ST)
*备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Semiparametric models provide a broad framework for statistical inference, yet efficient estimation typically relies on influence function correction tailored to each estimand and on nuisance estimation repeated for every sample. We show that a single pretrained Transformer can deliver efficient estimation and valid inference for a family of estimands in one forward pass, without deriving efficient influence functions or estimating nuisance functions. Pretrained on simulated data with the true parameter as the only label, the Transformer learns the posterior mean and covariance of the queried estimand and hence returns an estimate and a Wald-type confidence region. Theoretically, we prove that, for locally flat pretraining priors of slowly growing complexity, the posterior mean is efficient for every queried estimand. The Transformer inherits this efficiency with asymptotically exact coverage, in probability over evaluation populations and queries, even under distribution shift. We also reveal that the guarantee places much higher demands on pretraining when the data-generating distribution is fixed, as in classical frequentist inference. Experiments on causal inference, partial linear regression, and survival analysis show that the pretrained model generally achieves the lowest estimation error among competing methods, with nearly nominal coverage, at a computational cost of only about 0.02 seconds per dataset.

[LG-81] Block Search Conditioned on Features for Sequential Quantum Data Encoding CEC

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27587
作者: Cecília S. C. Botelho,Erico S. Teixeira,Anderson F. P. dos Santos,Guilherme D. Lima,Helida Santos,Adenauer Yamin,Renata Reiser,Inês de Castro Dutra
类目: Quantum Physics (quant-ph); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
*备注: 6 pages, 1 figure. Prepared for ESANN 2027. Code and reproduction scripts: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Sequential quantum data encoding is addressed through the joint selection of input features and encoding blocks within a fixed quantum register. At each step, a new feature, a block of operations, its placement, and its rotation weights are selected together from training data, extending the incremental construction of Q-FLAIR. With direct-loss selection (RAW), nine to twelve features were retained in four qubits across five new Bars and Stripes datasets. Under the same final calibration, mean changes relative to the calibrated Q-FLAIR reference were +5.53 percentage points in balanced accuracy, -15.83% in binary cross-entropy (BCE), and +7.79% in area under the ROC curve (AUC). The prespecified success criterion was met in four of five datasets and for the mean paired differences. These results were obtained by comparing complete procedures under a common cap of 32 operations.

[LG-82] Constraint-Aware Anticlustering Decomposition for Certifying Pairwise-Constrained Clustering

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27496
作者: Anna Livia Croella,Veronica Piccialli,Antonio M. Sudoso
类目: Optimization and Control (math.OC); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
*备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Certifying the quality of feasible solutions to large-scale minimum sum-of-squares clustering with pairwise must-link and cannot-link constraints remains challenging, as it requires strong lower bounds on the optimal objective value. We propose a decomposition framework that partitions the data points into smaller subsets, called anticlusters, and solves the induced clustering subproblems to obtain a certified optimality gap for the original problem. To preserve pairwise information, we introduce the Constrained Anticlustering Problem (CAP), which assigns each connected component of the constraint graph to a single anticluster while seeking geometrically representative subsets. We formulate CAP as a mixed-integer second-order cone program and develop a variable neighborhood search heuristic to construct high-quality decompositions. The resulting lower bound remains valid even when the induced subproblems are not solved to global optimality. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets with up to approximately 4,000 observations show that our approach can achieve mean optimality gaps below 1% at a modest computational cost.

[LG-83] Practical insights into controlling exponential concentration in quantum machine learning

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27486
作者: Fernando Mondragon-Sampedro,Diego Alvarez-Estevez
类目: Quantum Physics (quant-ph); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
*备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models are often limited by exponential concentration, where quantum observables become insensitive to input variations as system size increases. In this work, we provide a comparative empirical study of this phenomenon across Fidelity Quantum Kernels (FQK), Projected Quantum Kernels (PQK), and Quantum Extreme Learning (QEL), within a unified observable-based framework based on expectation-value variance. We investigate how measurement locality, entanglement, and circuit expressivity shape concentration across different architectures. Global fidelity-based kernels exhibit strong concentration driven by Hilbert space dimensionality, whereas local-observable approaches reduce but do not eliminate this effect. In PQK and QEL, concentration is primarily governed by entanglement and quantum dynamical expressivity, with reservoir depth emerging as a key factor in QEL architectures. We further study bandwidth scaling as a general mechanism for controlling encoding expressivity across all models. Our results indicate that bandwidth scaling effectively reduces concentration in moderate regimes by restricting the effective expressivity of the encoding, though this protective effect diminishes in highly expressive structural settings.

[LG-84] Neural variational Skyrmions as a topological benchmark: emergent symmetry precision energies and KAN–MLP comparison

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27411
作者: Koji Hashimoto,Masaki Murata,Gakuto Ogiwara
类目: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Nuclear Theory (nucl-th); Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)
*备注: 32 pages, 6 figures, 12 tables. Code and data: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:We propose the three-dimensional Skyrme model as a topological benchmark for neural variational methods and construct fully three-dimensional Skyrmions with baryon number B=1,\ldots,4 without imposing a symmetry ansatz, with high precision. For B=2,3,4 , the relaxation of these Skyrmions starts from B unit-charge lumps with random positions and orientations, which carry no symmetry information. The known toroidal, tetrahedral, and cubic Skyrmions nevertheless emerge spontaneously. The resulting variational energies for B=1,\ldots,4 lie slightly below the published reference values. The neural method highlights the high accuracy for retaining the topological charge, differing from B by at most 10^-6 in the highest-precision solutions. Our numerical method goes through physical constraint tests such as the Derrick virial relation and the Faddeev–Bogomolny bound, together with evaluation / verification through independent quadratures and resolution sweeps. We then compare Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KANs) with multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) in more than a thousand training runs, both with and without a rational-map ansatz. With default settings, KANs appear markedly superior, but most of the gap disappears once the MLP activation function and learning rate are tuned. KANs remain more parameter-efficient and more robust at fixed epoch budget, while MLPs with the tuned activation function perform at least as well at fixed wall-clock time. We also argue that continuous gradient descent cannot smoothly change the topological sector of our neural field, clarifying the origin of topological freezing observed in our neural variational solvers. Our results on the neural methods applied to Skyrmions pave a research ground for AI-agentic benchmarks for classical topological solitons, toward AI-assisted soliton physics.

[LG-85] Error-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Optimal Control of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles under Uncertainty

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27272
作者: Oliver Lundqvist,Fabricio Oliveira
类目: Optimization and Control (math.OC); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Systems and Control (eess.SY)
*备注: 26 pages including appendices, 2 figures, 10 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:We solve open-loop optimal control problems under parametric uncertainty using a physics-informed DeepONet that returns trajectories for all sampled scenarios in one evaluation. Trained only on the residual at generic controls, the operator is reused across targets and horizons. Because a gradient-based optimizer exploits surrogate errors, we correct the prediction by one Newton step on the dynamics, computed for all scenarios and times by one parallel scan. The corrected state has a second-order error bounded by the residual alone, and the corrected cost is honest for every control up to the sampling error. On a fixed-wing UAV benchmark, the corrected operator matches the accuracy of a batched Adam solver and an Ipopt solver at equal sample size and is 8 times faster than the Adam solver on the same GPU at a few hundred scenarios and 15 times faster than Ipopt on a CPU.

[LG-86] Semiparametric Efficiency for Entropic Optimal Transport under Structured Distribution Shift

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27261
作者: Yiming Ma,Weiwei Zhuang,Hang Liu
类目: Machine Learning (stat.ML); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
*备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Can structural information improve estimation of entropic optimal transport (EOT), and when is the gain zero? We study a fixed-dimensional exponential density ratio model (DRM) with a nonparametric baseline, compact support, and fixed positive regularization. At positive limiting sampling fractions, an exact projection identity quantifies the variance gain from the restriction. The pooled empirical-likelihood estimator attains the restricted bound and supports asymptotically valid confidence intervals when the bound is positive. Even under correct specification, the gain can be zero and can shrink as the tilt space expands. The same projection residual determines direction-specific first-order bias under local misspecification. When both samples grow and the target fraction vanishes, a zero first-order tilt derivative can leave source fluctuations and quadratic tilt error as the leading terms. Their balance gives a phase transition in the limiting distribution. A continuous example gives different convergence rates for two correctly specified bases at the same distribution pair. Controlled experiments assess the fixed-proportion theory. Natural-data comparisons distinguish variance reductions from improvements in reference RMSE driven by smaller reference bias.

[LG-87] Spectral Estimation with Deformed Decompression NEURIPS2026

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26945
作者: Siavash Ameli,Chris van der Heide,Liam Hodgkinson,Michael W. Mahoney
类目: Machine Learning (stat.ML); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Numerical Analysis (math.NA)
*备注: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Sample covariance matrices are fundamental objects in machine learning and statistics, with valuable information encoded into their eigenvalues. When treating modern problems, the scale of these matrices can become prohibitive for tractable computation. This creates a critical need for “spectral decompression”: a method for inferring the eigenspectrum of a very large-scale model using only information from its smaller realizations. Existing methods fall into two main categories: those relying on spectral inversion; and those that rely on Free Decompression techniques. On the one hand, spectral inversion is a fundamentally ill-posed problem that is notoriously unstable, often failing to yield reliable results in finite-size settings. On the other hand, while Free Decompression was recently proposed to address this scaling, its reliance on the Nica-Speicher framework restricts its use to unitarily invariant ensembles, a symmetry condition that subsampled covariance matrices fail to satisfy. In this work, we introduce Deformed Decompression (DD), a novel framework for the stable, forward-extrapolation of spectral densities. By leveraging properties of the companion matrix, DD recasts the spectral decompression problem as a directed evolution of the Stieltjes transform of the companion matrix. This approach bypasses the instabilities of traditional inversion and provides a robust methodology for scaling covariance matrices and even their generalized variants (including Hessian matrices) that lack unitary invariance. We demonstrate the utility of our framework through experiments on a variety of random matrix examples, showing that DD successfully captures the complex spectral signatures of large-scale systems.

[LG-88] Surface Cues Over Structure: Probing LLM Behavior on Brain Connectivity Graphs

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26913
作者: Prapti Roy,Khaled Mohammed Saifuddin
类目: Neurons and Cognition (q-bio.NC); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
*备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) provides a noninvasive view of functional interactions across the brain, which can be represented as connectivity graphs for neurological disease analysis. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being paired with such representations, yet it remains unclear whether they genuinely reason over the underlying connectivity or simply respond to surface-level cues that may trigger learned priors. We probe this question through a controlled study of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) diagnosis from resting-state functional connectivity, isolating one factor at a time to determine what drives an LLM’s predictions on brain connectivity graphs. Across six models, from small open-weight LLMs to a proprietary one, the same pattern holds: the results provide little evidence that predictions are consistently grounded in subject-specific connectivity. Brain region names, numeric formatting, and prompt framing shift what a model predicts without improving how well it separates ADHD subjects from Controls; perturbing the graph changes predictions no more for clinically meaningful regions than for random ones; and the models’ own justifications contradict the values they cite, inconsistently interpreting the connectivity evidence provided to them. Across every probe, predictions follow the model’s built-in class bias and the surface form of the prompt rather than the subject’s connectivity, calling into question a premise underlying current LLM brain integration work. Our code is available at this https URL.

[LG-89] Pharos: Learning to Control Rare Events at Scale

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26765
作者: Jiajun He,Jacky Chen,Weiliang Luo,Heather Kulik,David R. Koes,Carles Domingo-Enrich,Yuanqi Du
类目: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)
*备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Rare events drive transformations across physics, chemistry and biology, yet predicting their mechanisms and rates remains a fundamental challenge. Here we introduce Pharos, a framework that learns to make rare transitions accessible while predicting how frequently they occur under physical dynamics. Through stochastic optimal control, Pharos jointly learns the probability of completing a transition and how to steer simulations toward it, allowing sampling and learning to improve one another. Across biomolecular benchmarks, Pharos learns accurate transition probabilities with order-of-magnitude gains in convergence speed over previous algorithms. It transfers across ion assembly systems in explicit solvent while maintaining accurate reaction rate predictions, scales to host-guest binding systems that span millisecond timescales, and enables chemical reaction studies with a computationally demanding machine learning interatomic potential. By combining efficient sampling, quantitative kinetics, and transferability, Pharos opens a route toward foundation models of rare event mechanisms and rates across molecular systems.

[LG-90] Distributional Deep Hedging

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26652
作者: El-Amine Cherrat,Skander Kazdaghli,Iordanis Kerenidis
类目: Computational Finance (q-fin.CP); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Risk Management (q-fin.RM)
*备注: 34 pages, 7 figures, 12 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Deep hedging learns a hedging strategy by optimising a risk preference over a neural-network policy. The preference is fixed before training, so each new preference requires a new policy and, in actor-critic methods, a new critic. We propose distributional deep hedging, in which the distribution of the hedging profit and loss is learned through its quantiles and the risk preference is applied afterwards, as a weight on those quantiles. We characterise the preferences that admit this representation, which include expected shortfall and its mixtures, and show that the entropic utility is computed from the same quantiles. At the current policy, each of these preferences is bounded below by an expected utility with the same gradient. This bound reduces risk-sensitive hedging to a sequence of risk-neutral problems, from which we derive policy-search and actor-critic algorithms. In numerical experiments, the learned hedges approach references computed by dynamic programming, and a single distributional critic trained without a preference can serve preferences chosen after training.

[LG-91] o predict or to persist: how decoherence shapes learning in a spin-qubit quantum reservoir

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26215
作者: Nikolaos Petropoulos,Elena Blokhina
类目: Quantum Physics (quant-ph); Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall); Emerging Technologies (cs.ET); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Chaotic Dynamics (nlin.CD)
*备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:In this work we investigate how dephasing and the choice of measured observables affect learning in a simulated six-qubit spin chain with Markovian dissipation and exact expectation-value readout. For externally driven nonlinear autoregressive moving-average signals, combining single- and two-qubit observables gives better predictions than a population-only readout at comparable polynomial feature counts. Most of the configurations we tested become more accurate than a reference with relaxation and dephasing disabled, most strongly at T_2=1,\mu s, where total memory capacity drops, and still at T_2=5 - 10,\mu s, where memory is only redistributed across delays. For autonomous generation, we train the readout with scheduled sampling and iterative dataset aggregation to expose it to states reached under its own feedback. We do not find a clear systematic dependence of limit-cycle persistence on coherence across the reservoir ensemble. For chaotic forecasting, in contrast, prediction horizons at T_2=1,\mu s shorten in all 10 reservoir realizations relative to that reference. For the noise-driven strange non-chaotic attractor, the model produces a smooth, approximately closed orbit, and neither captures the target’s scatter nor follows its trajectory pointwise. We conclude that, within this simulated reservoir, the impact of coherence depends strongly on the task.

[LG-92] Cup and Cap Topological Neural Network

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03169
作者: Marta Niedostatek,Ferran Hernandez Caralt,Runyue Wang,Federica Baccini,Lorenzo Giambagli,Pietro Lió,Ginestra Bianconi
类目: Disordered Systems and Neural Networks (cond-mat.dis-nn); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
*备注: 9 pages, 1 table + appendices

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Topological Deep Learning (TDL) is designed to learn features associated not only with nodes but also with edges, triangles and higher dimensional simplices. However, most TDL approaches, being based on boundary operators and Hodge Laplacians, have the limitation that features and signals cannot be lifted or lowered across more than one dimension per layer. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we propose the adoption of the cup and cap products. Specifically, we formulate the Cup and Cap Topological Neural Network (CCNN), a topological deep learning architecture designed to learn node-based variables (or 0-cochains) by taking into account their many-body interactions (e.g. triangles) present in the data. We validate CCNN by assessing its performance on the TopoBench datasets, demonstrating its competitive performance with respect to other simplicial complex neural networks.
